newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: More troops depart to protect Portuguese in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: More troops depart to protect Portuguese in Zaire.

text.p: A senior official urged the estimated 400 Portuguese nationals in war-torn Zaire to leave the country on Wednesday as a further group of crack troops prepared to leave on a mission to protect Portuguese citizens.
"While it is possible to leave Kinshasa voluntarily, I appeal to the Portuguese to leave," said Jose Lello, Secretary of State for Portuguese Communities.
"We consider that there are strong possibilities that public order will deteriorate in Kinshasa," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

He said some 30 special forces rangers would leave for Congo on Wednesday afternoon and a group of 40 infantry had left on Tuesday to reinforce the Portuguese soldiers already sent to protect nationals in Zaire.
The latest departures will bring the total Portuguese military contingent to 140, including doctors and other medical staff, all of them volunteers, Lello said.
South African President Nelson Mandela arrived in Congo on Wednesday for last-chance talks to unite Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila on a peace plan.
Lello estimated that dozens of Portuguese residents had already left Kinshasa since the Portuguese government issued a first appeal to them on Monday to leave the country.

"We are keeping track of the Portuguese as closely as we can so that we have a good idea of how many may have to be evacuated. Some Portuguese have already left for Angola and Brazzaville (Congo)," he said.
Lello said at least 100 Portuguese nationals, many of them businessmen, had chosen to remain in Zaire. "More than 100 Portuguese want to stay. They don't want to abandon their businesses," he said.
Portuguese officials have said that if the situation deteriorated, the Portuguese would head for designated "welcome centres" from where they would be taken to the Portuguese embassy.
They would then cross the Zaire river to Brazzaville, Congo's capital, guarded by the soldiers.
Any decision to evacuate Portuguese nationals would follow a signal from the Portuguese ambassador in Kinshasa and final word from the defence and foreign ministries in Lisbon, Lello said.
U.S., French, Belgian and British troops are also on standby to evacuate foreign nationals from Kinshasa in the event of a battle for the city or a rampage by Zaire's ragged and ill-disciplined army.
Several thousand Western nationals live in Zaire's capital, mainly citizens of France and the former colonial power, Belgium. The United States has 400 nationals there, Canada 500.
